title: Money Is a Story We All Agree to Believe
subtitle: The cash in your pocket is worthless paper. The number in your bank isn't even paper. So why does the whole world chase it?
hook: Pull out a banknote. It's a rectangle of cotton worth basically nothing. The balance in your bank isn't even *that* — it's a number in a database. Yet people trade years of their lives for these things. Weird, right? Here's the punchline: money was never a *thing*. It's a **technology** — invented to kill one specific, maddening problem. Once you see the problem, money makes total sense. Lesson one of Money & Markets.

sections.heading: The problem that almost broke trade
sections.body:
Picture a world with no money — just barter. You make shoes; you want bread. So you must find a baker who wants shoes *and* happens to have spare bread *right now*. Economists call this the **double coincidence of wants**, and it's a nightmare. Most trades simply never happen, because the perfect match is too rare.

Money is the hack. If everyone accepts *one thing*, you sell shoes to anyone, then buy bread from anyone. One impossible trade becomes two easy ones. That's the entire invention — everything else is detail.

sections.caption: Barter needs a perfect mutual match (rare!). Money splits the deal so each side only needs to find someone who wants what they've got.

sections.heading: Money's three day-jobs
sections.body:
Stop asking *what* money is and ask what it *does*. Three jobs:

- **Medium of exchange** — the thing everyone takes (kills the barter problem).
- **Unit of account** — a shared ruler, so you can compare a car to a coffee.
- **Store of value** — it (mostly) holds worth over time, so you can sell today and buy next year.

Do those three jobs and you *are* money. Cattle, salt, shells, gold, paper, database numbers — all have taken a turn. Good money is just whatever does the jobs well: durable, splittable, portable, hard to fake, and — the big one — trusted.

sections.label: The plot twist: it's all trust
sections.body: Modern money isn't backed by gold. A banknote is backed by everyone's shared belief that *someone else will take it tomorrow*, propped up by a government that can tax and enforce. Money is a collective story. Sounds flimsy — but that's exactly its strength: its value lives in the network of people who believe, not in the stuff it's printed on.

sections.caption: From shells and coins to paper and pixels — a quick tour of money's glow-up.

sections.label: Tomorrow's cliffhanger
sections.body: If money is a store of value across *time*, here's the trillion-dollar question: is a dollar today worth the same as a dollar next year? (Spoiler: absolutely not — and that one crack cracks open interest, loans, and the price of literally every investment.)

takeaways: Money is a **technology**, not a substance — it kills the 'double coincidence of wants'.
It turns one impossible trade into two easy ones: sell to anyone, buy from anyone.
Its three jobs: **medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value**.
Anything doing those jobs can be money; good money is durable, divisible, portable, hard to fake, trusted.
Modern money runs on **trust + law**, not gold — value lives in the network of believers.

quiz.q: What problem was money invented to solve?
options: The 'double coincidence of wants' in barter
quiz.explain: In barter you need someone who has what you want AND wants what you have. Money removes that near-impossible match.

quiz.q: Which is NOT one of money's three jobs?
quiz.explain: The three are exchange, account, and store of value. Interest is a *consequence* — tomorrow's lesson.

quiz.q: BOSS: If a country's people suddenly stopped believing their banknotes would be accepted tomorrow, what happens to the money's value?
options: It collapses, because its value was the shared belief itself
quiz.explain: Modern money is a shared story. Break the belief and the value evaporates — exactly how hyperinflations spiral.

tg_quiz.q: What actually backs a modern banknote?
options: Shared trust that others will accept it
tg_quiz.correct: Exactly — money is a story we all agree to believe.
tg_quiz.wrong: Not gold — it's collective trust, backed by law.
tg_quiz.explain: Value lives in the network of people who accept it, not the paper.
